sentences.text: Faecalimonas umbilicata is an obligately anaerobic, non-spore-forming, Gram-stain-positive cocco-bacillus of the family Lachnospiraceae, isolated from human faeces and forming characteristic umbilicated colonies on EG agar.
Its DNA G+C content was reported as 46.9 and 45.5 mol% for the two strains, with major cellular fatty acids C18:1ω9c, C16:0 and C18:1ω9c dimethyl acetal.

A study reported that Faecalimonas umbilicata was significantly enriched in the gut microbiota of patients with post-stroke cognitive impairment compared with healthy controls, and negatively correlated with MMSE and MoCA scores.

In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial in patients with mild to moderate Crohn's disease, Faecalimonas umbilicata was among short chain fatty acid producing bacteria that increased in fecal samples.
